label: D1 update gate dips after a1->S2 rare trials and steeply in the last ~10 trials
terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_action == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 85, 0)**3 ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 85, 0)**3 ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_action == 1) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 80, 0) ;; (phase == D1) * value * np.maximum(ep_trial - 85, 0)**2 ;; (phase != D1) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 85, 0)**3
explanation: Raw update gate z of unit 47 sits near 1 (mean 0.997). Nearly all its variance is at D1. (1) Whether the previous trial was a1 then rare S2 matters: z drops about 0.013-0.02 at D1 after that, whichever the reward. After any S1 outcome it goes up slightly (+0.004), and after a2->S2 it is near baseline. So it tracks the last choice x reached state (an a1/S2 mismatch), not reward. (2) A steep within-decile collapse in the last ~10-15 episode trials (z down to ~0.8 at D1) that the decile baseline misses. The cubic ramp terms capture it with about the same weight after rewarded and unrewarded trials. The a1->S2 dip deepens late in the episode, and at D1 higher model value softens the late dip. GO/D2 get only a small late ramp. Previous-trial table alone gives 0.30 and the additive all-cue ceiling is 0.34, so a large part of this score comes from the within-decile episode-time interactions. Test R^2 beyond timing 0.63 (dev 0.63). Uses no future variables. Value is a model-internal quantity.

issues: The late-episode collapse is mostly a growth of the previous-trial effect, not a separate collapse that applies whatever the history. Per-decile fits of the a1->S2 dip: about -0.010 in deciles 0-5, -0.019 in decile 7, -0.031 in decile 8 and -0.073 in decile 9. The prev-trial table plus an a1S2*ramp(ep_trial-80) term scores 0.550 test. Adding a generic D1 late cubic on top gives only 0.553.

The rise after S1 outcomes also grows sharply late in the episode: +0.002 in deciles 0-5, +0.004 in decile 7, +0.007 in decile 8, +0.021 in decile 9. The explanation calls it a flat +0.004, and the terms have no S1 x time interaction. Adding (phase==D1)*(prev_state==1)*ramp(ep_trial-80) to the original terms raises test R^2 from 0.625 to 0.682, a systematic gap.

The claim that the late dip is 'about equal after rewarded and unrewarded trials' only holds once the value*late^2 term is in the model. Without value, the late cubic weight after unrewarded trials is about 4x larger (-5.1e-6 vs -1.3e-6). The two reward-split cubics and value*late^2 work only together: removing both cubics leaves 0.554, and value*late^2 with a single cubic gives 0.624. The value terms on their own score 0.04. So (2) is really 'late D1 dip deeper at low model value', not a reward-blind collapse.

Adding a late term for rare previous transitions (prev_common==0)*late^2 to the original terms gives 0.653, with a positive weight: rare outcomes soften the late dip. The explanation does not mention this.

The worst-fit windows that remain are isolated, sharp late D1 dips (z about 0.80-0.85 at t92-t99) that no previous-trial pattern predicts. Errors by phase x previous trial are small (|mean| <= 0.002), so this residual is scattered rather than a missed category.
The other claims check out on test: a1->S2 dip whatever the reward (-0.0206/-0.0204), a near-baseline value after a2->S2, no future variables used, and only a small late ramp at GO/D2.
